title: Dynamic Answer Eval Suite and Calibration Guidelines
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This document describes the Dynamic Answer Evaluation Suite (DAES), a structured set of tests and calibration steps designed to measure and improve the stability, calibration, and content fidelity of generation models across small prompt perturbations, paraphrases, and configuration sweeps. DAES is intended to be used by model onboarding, continuous eval, and regression-triage workflows to prevent regressions that are invisible to single-shot metrics.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers onboarding models for serving
- QA and SRE teams running regression triage
- Product owners tracking release readiness

Goals:
- Quantify answer stability under paraphrase and prompt-variant perturbations
- Measure model calibration (confidence vs. accuracy) and reduce overconfidence
- Provide a reproducible promotion gate and alerting thresholds for model rollout
- Supply actionable remediation steps (calibration, temperature, prompt templates)

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: text generation tasks where a single canonical answer or small set of acceptable answers exists (FAQ responses, knowledge-grounded replies, short-form summarization).
- Non-goals: open-ended creative generation evaluation (poetry, fiction) — those use complementary subjective eval suites.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Reproducibility Score (RS): fraction of perturbation variants that produce an answer semantically equivalent to the canonical answer set. Computed via semantic-similarity (embedding cosine >= 0.86) or exact-match for short answers.
- Expected Calibration Error (ECE): binning-based calibration metric on per-token or per-answer confidence.
- Entropy Drift (ED): average change in response-token entropy between baseline prompt and perturbed prompt variants.
- Prefix Sensitivity Index (PSI): score measuring how different answers are when canonical prefix text is added/removed (range 0–1 where 0 is insensitive).

Test matrix (high-level):
1) Paraphrase Stability: 20 paraphrase variants per canonical prompt (mix of rule-based and synthetic paraphrases). Compute RS, ECE, ED.
2) Prompt Template Sensitivity: 8 templated variants (politeness changes, instruction-first vs. question-first).
3) Temperature Sweep: run T = [0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8] for each variant to expose distribution changes.
4) Context Perturbation: insert distractor sentences upstream and downstream to measure PSI.
5) Adversarial Noise: character-level and semantic noise at 5%/10% rates to test stability.

Procedure: running DAES locally or in CI
1. Data selection
  a. Choose 500 to 2,000 canonical QA items representative of target workload (see "Dataset curation checklist" below).
  b. Reserve a held-out set (10%) for regression validation.
2. Variant generation
  a. Generate 20 paraphrases per item using the paraphrase-service pipeline (service: paraphrase-runner v1.3).
  b. Add template variants using the prompt-template library (repo: redwood/prompt-templates).
3. Harness execution
  a. Use eval-harness CLI: eval-harness run --suite daes --config daes-config.yaml --parallelism 48
  b. For Hosted API runs, set routing to dedicated-test-queue to avoid quota impact.
  c. Record per-request metadata: model_id, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, temperature, seed, variant_id.
4. Scoring and aggregation
  a. Compute per-item RS, ECE (5 bins), ED, PSI.
  b. Aggregate by workload slice (domain, average prompt length, language).
  c. Attach CPU/GPU utilization and KV-cache hit-rate metadata where available.
5. Promotion gate
  a. Gate passes when: median RS >= 0.90, ECE <= 0.08, and PSI <= 0.12 for targeted workload slices.
  b. If any critical slice (high-traffic customer slice) fails thresholds, block promotion and create a triage ticket.

Dataset curation checklist (table):
| Field | Requirement | Rationale |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| Size | 500–2,000 items | Balance statistical power with CI runtime |
| Diversity | At least 6 domains & 3 style buckets | Avoid overfitting to narrow prompts |
| Answer type | Short factual, single-sentence, or bounded list | DAES assumes limited answer variability |
| Reference answers | 1–3 canonical answers per item | Needed for RS computation |
| Annotations | difficulty, domain, sensitivity flag | For slice-based analysis |

Example config (daes-config.yaml):
```yaml
suite: daes
paraphrase_count: 20
temperatures: [0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8]
batch_size: 64
parallelism: 48
scoring: [rs, ece, entropy_drift, psi]
thresholds:
  rs: 0.90
  ece: 0.08
  psi: 0.12
slices: [domain, prompt_length_bucket, customer_tier]
logging:
  destination: s3://redwood-evals/daes/results/${run_id}.ndjson
  include_request_meta: true
```

Scoring details and implementation notes:
- RS (Reproducibility Score): compute pairwise semantic similarity against canonical answer set using embedding service (service: embeddings-v2) and a cosine threshold 0.86. For short numeric answers prefer exact-match before embedding fallback.
- ECE: implement using 10 bins by default for per-answer confidence. For LLMs without native answer-level confidence, derive confidence as mean token-level softmax exp(logits) normalized score; document the derivation in the run metadata.
- Entropy Drift: compute token-level entropy distribution and report mean absolute change.

Alerting and dashboards:
- Dashboards: "DAES: Stability Overview" (Grafana) showing RS trend, ECE distribution, PSI heatmap by slice.
- Alerts: triggered when 3 consecutive runs show RS drop >= 3% on any critical slice OR ECE rises above 0.12. Alerts page: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/alerting/daes-alerts (create ticket to link).

Remediation playbook (first-pass):
1. Reproduce locally with the failing slice and the exact run_id.
2. Run a focused temperature sweep and 1k-sample bootstrap to estimate variance.
3. If ECE high: try temperature=0.0 baseline, then consider post-hoc calibration (temperature scaling on logits using held-out calibration set).
4. If RS low and PSI high: evaluate whether prompt templates are inconsistent; attempt prompt-simplification and prefix normalization.
5. For regressions introduced after quantization: run quantization-compatibility check (see quantization-profiles/kv-cache-quant-stability-audit-playbook-2025) and increase quant precision on critical response heads.

Promotion ticket template (what to include):
- run_id, model_id, model_version
- failing slice(s) and metric deltas vs baseline
- attached ndjson results link and salient examples (5 failing items)
- suggested next steps and owner

Integration with regression triage:
- Add DAES run to the nightly regression matrix; if DAES flags a regression it should automatically attach to the weekly "model-regression-forensics" board (Kanban).
- For high-severity customer-facing regressions, page a SE on-call and create a cross-functional postmortem if rollback occurs.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- DAES harness maintenance: applied-ml team (owners: @maya.patel, @arjun.rao)
- Paraphrase pipeline maintenance: nlp-data team (owner: @elena.fischer)
- Dashboards & alerting: observability team (owner: @samir.khan)
- Onboarding gate enforcement: model-onboarding board (owner: product-ml lead)

Operational cost and runtime guidance:
- Typical run (1,000 items, paraphrase_count=20, temps=4) costs ~ 0.8–1.2 GPU-hours on p4d-equivalent (measurement from q3-2025).
- Use sampling mode for early preflight checks (paraphrase_count=5) to reduce cost.

FAQ:
Q: Why use embeddings for RS instead of string match?
A: Embeddings capture semantic equivalence across lexical variants and are robust to minor syntactic differences; exact-match is brittle for short paraphrases.

Q: How often should we run DAES?
A: Nightly on the primary model branch; full-suite weekly for production candidates.

Q: When should we block promotion?
A: If any critical customer slice fails the RS/ECE/PSI thresholds or if multiple slices degrade simultaneously (see Promotion gate).
